subject: Azure private offer — SKU discount schedule and partner split
messages:
From: Kari Jensen <kari.jensen@datascale.com>
To: mateo.alvarez@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Azure private offer — SKU discount schedule and partner split

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for taking a look. We're preparing a private offer request for Azure Marketplace and want to confirm a few things before we send a formal PO:

- Target committed spend: $480k over 12 months (broken across three SKUs).
- DSC request: A flat discount off list at SKU level, and a separate line showing the pass-through (channel) margin we can pay our reseller. Our reseller requires at least a 7% pass-through to maintain their margin.
- Can Redwood expose SKU-level unit prices in the private offer and reserve the committed capacity for the quarter?

Attached is a short requirements spreadsheet showing SKU splits and usage profiles. Also, if you could share a sample proforma or the SKU mapping you use for Azure private offers that would help speed our procurement.

Kari
Kari Jensen
Head of Procurement, DataScale Corp
Attachments: DSC_Azure_Requirements.xlsx (xlsx)

From: mateo.alvarez@redwood.com
To: Kari Jensen <kari.jensen@datascale.com>, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-21T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Azure private offer — SKU discount schedule and partner split

Hi Kari — thanks, got the spreadsheet. Looping in Ben and Vanessa to confirm channel pass-through and SKU mapping for Azure private offers. A few quick answers:

- We can publish SKU-level unit prices in the private offer and apply reserved capacity for the committed period (we'll need the PO to lock the commitment).
- Typical starting discount for an order of this size is 12% off list. Channel pass-through (what we can show as "reseller share") is configurable — we usually carve out a separate commission line (6–10% typical depending on partner tier).

Ben/Vanessa — can you confirm whether 7% pass-through is dealable here and whether we need any special marketplace SKUs or bundling to keep the list/discount math tidy? I'm attaching a quick SKU mapping CSV I use for these requests.

Next steps: we'll respond with a draft private offer (with SKU lines) and a DocuSign PO template for your procurement team to review.

Thanks,
Mateo Alvarez
Sr. Strategic Sales Manager | Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: mateo.alvarez@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-21T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Azure private offer — SKU discount schedule and partner split

Mateo / Vanessa —

7% pass-through requirement is within range, but we need to decide how to show it externally vs. internally for reporting:

Option A: Show a single discounted line on the private offer and issue a separate reseller invoice that reflects the 7% commission. Cleaner for marketplace billing, but means partner margin isn't visible in the offer.

Option B: Include a dedicated "Reseller pass-through" SKU line at the bottom of the private offer (negative price) so the reseller margin is explicit in the DocuSign PO. This is visible to the buyer and reseller.

Operational notes:
- For Option B we need Finance to approve negative-line handling in marketplace settlements (I'll loop them).
- If we go with Option A, Laura on Marketplace should confirm that Azure will accept the single-line PV (private offer) and downstream reseller invoice flow.

I'm fine starting at 12% list discount + explicit 7% reseller pass-through (Option B) if Finance okays it. If buyer pushes back we can offer 15% list discount with 6% pass-through as a counter.

Attaching: proforma-sku-mapping.csv for Mateo to send along.

-Ben
Principal Sales Ops
Attachments: proforma-sku-mapping.csv (csv)

From: Kari Jensen <kari.jensen@datascale.com>
To: mateo.alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: Samir Rao <samir@datascale.com>
Date: 2026-05-21T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Azure private offer — SKU discount schedule and partner split

Thanks Mateo — and thanks Ben for the options. A couple of clarifications from DSC:

- Our procurement prefers the reseller margin shown on the PO (Option B) so our reseller can reconcile quickly.
- DataScale needs clarity on net vs gross pricing for internal budgeting; can you provide both the list-to-discount math and the final net after reseller pass-through?
- Our target is to secure a 20% off list effective discount at the committed level after all negotiations; however, we can accept a split: 15% list discount + 5% reseller pass-through if Redwood can commit to reserved capacity and a firm 12-month pricing window.

We have a working draft PO ready to attach — sending it now for completeness. Hoping we can get a counter by tomorrow so our legal/procurement can move quickly.

Kari
Attachments: Draft_PO.docx (docx)

From: mateo.alvarez@redwood.com
To: Kari Jensen <kari.jensen@datascale.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-22T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Azure private offer — SKU discount schedule and partner split

Kari — appreciate the fast turnaround. Internal quick update and proposal:

- Committed capacity: we can set a reserved capacity window for the 12 months once PO is executed, with quarterly usage true-ups.
- Pricing proposal (counter): 15% off list applied at SKU level + explicit 8% reseller pass-through line (Option B). This gets you closer to your 20% effective target while giving the reseller visible margin.
- We'll produce the private offer with SKU lines and include both gross (list) and net (after discount & pass-through) columns for transparency.

Next steps:
1) I'll prepare the private offer draft and upload the DocuSign envelope.
2) Ben will confirm Finance sign-off on negative-line handling (should be done by EOD).
3) Kari, if you can confirm the exact PO billing contact and the reseller legal entity name, we'll map names on the DocuSign.

I'll send the private-offer link and the finalized DocuSign in a follow-up email.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Sr. Strategic Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
